world.setting: A small Indiana town and its high school; two teenagers meet on the ledge of the school bell tower and spend the rest of the book wandering the state.

finch.name: Theodore Finch
finch.look: a lanky American teenage boy with dark messy hair, a black t-shirt and a battered jacket, restless, present day

violet.name: Violet Markey
violet.look: an American teenage girl with long blonde hair, a cardigan over a school dress, holding herself carefully, present day

embry.name: Mr Embry
embry.look: a short, thickset middle-aged American school counsellor in a rumpled shirt and tie, built like a bull

amanda.name: Amanda Monk
amanda.look: an American teenage girl in cheerleader colours, immaculate, watching who is watching

classroom.look: Mr Black's US Geography room, wall map, desks in rows

bedroom.look: Finch's room with the wall of Post-it notes he rearranges at night

highway.look: Indiana two-lane roads between wandering sites, flat fields either side

office.look: the school counsellor's small office, one window, two chairs too close together

objects.why: the bell tower ledge is where they meet and where the book returns - its single central image
the institution that labels both of them and helps neither
Finch's Post-it wall and the Wander notes - how he thinks out loud
the Blue Hole - the book's last place, and the one it refuses to explain
Wander Indiana: the project is a road trip, and the road is the relationship

spine.claim: Two teenagers save each other in the wrong direction on a bell tower.
A school project becomes the only structure either of them has.
Every institution around them optimises for its own risk, not for the kid in front of it.
The illness did not make him deep; it killed the depth he already had.
